items.followUp: Why is a prototype useful before developing the final solution?

rubric.why: Shows that a prototype is an early representation of the proposed solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as an early or preliminary model of the solution.

rubric.why: States a practical benefit of using a prototype during planning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit, such as getting feedback, finding problems early, or saving time or cost.

modelAnswer: A prototype is an early model of a proposed solution.
It helps test the idea, get feedback, and find problems before developing the final solution, saving time and cost.

items.followUp: Name the five questions used to analyse a problem.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the names of the five Ws.
rubric.description: Names any three of the five Ws.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any three distinct correct names.

rubric.why: The complete set contains five questions used to analyse a problem.
rubric.description: Names the remaining two Ws to complete the set.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer gives the complete set of five distinct Ws.

modelAnswer: Who?
What?
Where?
When?
Why?

items.followUp: What is decision making in problem solving?

rubric.why: Captures the central act of decision making: choosing among possibilities.
rubric.description: Defines decision making as choosing an option.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a choice is made from available options or alternatives.

rubric.why: A decision is made by evaluating options against relevant conditions or requirements.
rubric.description: Explains the basis for the choice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that the choice depends on conditions, criteria, information, or requirements.

modelAnswer: Decision making is the process of choosing the most suitable option from available alternatives.
The choice is made by considering the conditions or requirements of the problem.

rubric.why: Identifies HTML's defining type as a markup language.
rubric.description: Identifies HTML as a markup language.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming HTML as a markup language.

rubric.why: A characteristic of HTML is that tags structure webpage content for display in a browser.
rubric.description: Gives a further characteristic of HTML.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it uses tags to create or structure webpages, or that a browser displays HTML pages.

modelAnswer: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is a markup language used to create and structure web pages.
It uses tags to describe webpage content, which is displayed by a web browser.

items.followUp:
What text will be displayed by this HTML paragraph: `

rubric.why: Checks the exact text contained in the paragraph element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the text shown between the paragraph tags.

rubric.why: Shows that the paragraph tags format the text and are not displayed as page content.
rubric.description: Identifies the text as a paragraph, not HTML tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or showing that the output is a paragraph and the tags themselves are not displayed.

modelAnswer: My First Paragraph

rubric.why: The first division gives the least significant hexadecimal digit.
rubric.description: Shows the first division and remainder.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly obtaining remainder 2 from 786 divided by 16.

rubric.why: Reading the remainders from last to first gives the hexadecimal result 312.
rubric.description: Completes the conversion and gives the hexadecimal answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct remaining remainders and final answer (312)₁₆.

modelAnswer: Given: (786)₁₀
786 ÷ 16 = 49 remainder 2
49 ÷ 16 = 3 remainder 1
3 ÷ 16 = 0 remainder 3
Read the remainders from bottom to top: (786)₁₀ = (312)₁₆

items.followUp: Explain the function of the AND operator.

rubric.why: NOT is a logical operator that acts on one Boolean value and reverses it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying NOT as a logical (unary) operator that complements a value.

rubric.why: The defining behaviour of NOT is to reverse a Boolean value.
rubric.description: States the effect of NOT on truth values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that true becomes false and false becomes true.

modelAnswer: NOT is a logical unary operator that reverses a Boolean value.
It changes TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE.

items.followUp: What is volatile memory? Give one example.

accept: keeps data when power is off
data remains when power is off
rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains stored information when electrical power is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it retains data when the power is off.

rubric.why: A correct example supports the definition of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid non-volatile memory or storage device.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its stored data even when the power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.
